name: Lightweight Sitemap Generator
author: andreyberestov

sections.description:
Lightweight Sitemap Generator is a minimal yet powerful WordPress plugin that creates a valid XML sitemap for search engines (Google, Yandex and others), fully compliant with sitemaps.org.

The plugin follows the “set it and forget it” philosophy: minimal settings, maximum reliability.

Main features:
– Generates a valid XML sitemap (sitemap.xml) with <loc> and <lastmod> tags in strict ISO-8601 UTC format
– Two working modes:
– File mode (sitemap.xml in site root) — lowest server load, requires write permissions
– Dynamic mode (on-the-fly) — sitemap is always up to date, no file is created (slightly higher server load)
– Simple settings page in WP Admin:
– Include static pages (page) — enabled by default
– Include posts (post) — enabled by default
– Include categories — disabled by default
– Include tags — disabled by default
– Include date archives — disabled by default
– Include author archives — disabled by default
– Include questions (plugin DW Question Answer ≥ 1.4.3.4) — disabled by default
– Include products (WooCommerce ≥ 2.6) — disabled by default, supports simple and grouped products
– Include any detected custom post types and custom taxonomies — disabled by default, can be enabled individually
– Homepage is always included automatically (no duplicates)
– Flexible for homepage:
– Smart — based on the latest modified posts, pages, WooCommerce products, DW Q&A entries, and any enabled custom post types
– Conservative — uses the modified date of the static front page (if set)
– Now — always uses the current time (updates on every sitemap generation)
– Split large sitemaps into parts (up to 50,000 URLs each), with automatic sitemapindex
– Conflict detection with popular sitemap plugins (Yoast SEO, All in One SEO Pack, Rank Math, The SEO Framework, SEOPress, Google XML Sitemaps)
– File mode: permission check for writing sitemap.xml into site root
– Dynamic mode: admin notice if a physical sitemap.xml file exists (to avoid conflicts) + diagnostic header X-LWSGP-Mode: dynamic
– Displays date & time of the last file sitemap generation (user can choose between UTC (GMT+0) or site timezone for display; note: this affects only the “Last generated” info line, not the <lastmod> tags inside the sitemap)
– Security:
– Capability checks (manage_options)
– Nonce validation
– Sanitization & whitelisting of options
– File operations via WP_Filesystem (with safe fallback)
– Inline CSS only, no extra assets, no external calls — minimal and robust

Credits

Created by Andrey Berestov
sections.installation:
1. Upload the plugin folder to /wp-content/plugins/ or install via Plugins → Add New.
  2. Activate the plugin in the WordPress admin.
  3. A new menu item Lightweight Sitemap will appear in the admin sidebar. Open it, configure the options you need, and click Generate / Update sitemap.
  4. Your sitemap will be available at: https://example.com/sitemap.xml
sections.faq:
I see a conflict warning with another SEO plugin. Should I worry?

No. The conflict check is purely informational. It just means that another plugin is also generating an XML sitemap.
In most cases you can simply disable sitemap generation in that plugin (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress, etc.).
This does not affect your site’s performance or indexing; it’s just to help avoid confusion.

Will it work with future WordPress and PHP versions?

Yes. The plugin is written in a simple, standards-compliant way. It supports PHP 7.0 and above (tested up to 8.4) and WordPress from 6.2 up to 6.8.2.

Does it work on older WordPress / PHP versions?

The plugin code is written in a very simple, standards-compliant way and was originally tested to work even on PHP 5.6 and WordPress 4.8.
However, to comply with the current WordPress.org Plugin Directory requirements, the officially supported versions are PHP 7.0+ and WordPress 6.2+.
If you run an older site, the plugin may still work, but we recommend updating to a supported environment for security and performance.

Why both “file” and “dynamic” modes?

  • File mode: minimal server load, recommended if your hosting allows writing to site root.
  • Dynamic mode: sitemap is always fresh, works without file write permissions, but server load is slightly higher.

Why doesn’t the plugin split the sitemap into multiple files by category (like the default WordPress sitemap)?

The native WordPress sitemap (/wp-sitemap.xml) generates multiple files for posts, pages, categories, tags, and other objects.
This structure is not wrong, but it makes things more complex without real SEO benefit.

According to the official sitemaps.org specification and search engine documentation (Google, Yandex, Bing), there is no ranking or indexing advantage in splitting by taxonomy.
Search engines only care that:
– All important URLs are listed.
– Each URL has a correct <loc> and (optionally) <lastmod>.
– The sitemap is valid XML and under the 50,000 URL / 50 MB per file limit.

The plugin keeps one clean sitemap (with automatic split into parts only when necessary). This avoids clutter, reduces confusion for users, and keeps things minimal yet powerful.

Why doesn’t the plugin include “priority” or “changefreq” tags?

These optional fields (<priority> and <changefreq>) were part of the early sitemap protocol but are ignored by all major search engines today.
– Google officially states that these values are not used for crawling or ranking decisions.
– Yandex also ignores them and relies only on <loc> and <lastmod>.

Including these tags gives a false sense of control without actual effect. That’s why the plugin follows the modern standard: only <loc> and <lastmod> are included, which is exactly what search engines expect and trust.

How does the “Smart” homepage mode behave on static landing pages?

The “Smart” mode checks for the most recent changes among posts, products, or Q&A entries (if enabled).
If your site is a static landing page without posts, WooCommerce products, or DW Q&A content, there are simply no dynamic sources to check.
In that case, “Smart” mode automatically falls back to the modification time of the homepage itself — exactly like a “conservative” mode.

This means you don’t need an extra setting:
– On blogs or shops, reflects the freshest content.
– On static landing pages, updates only when the homepage page itself is edited.

Which plugins are supported?

  • WooCommerce (version 2.6 and above) — simple & grouped products
  • DW Question Answer (version 1.4.3.4 and above) — published Q&A pages
  • Any plugin that registers a public custom post type or public custom taxonomy — detected automatically.
    This means the plugin can support almost any third-party extension (portfolio plugins, directory listings, events, job boards, and more), as long as the post type or taxonomy is registered in WordPress as public.

How is security handled?

  • Admin-only access (capability check)
  • wp_nonce protection for all actions
  • Escaping output
  • File operations via WP_Filesystem with safe fallback

How can I verify that dynamic mode works?

Open https://yoursite.com/sitemap.xml in browser developer tools or run:

curl -I https://yoursite.com/sitemap.xml

You should see the header X-LWSGP-Mode: dynamic in the response.
If a physical sitemap.xml file exists in the site root, the server may serve it directly (without headers). The plugin will show a warning in the admin panel and let you delete that file.

Do I need to edit robots.txt?

The plugin does not touch your robots.txt automatically.
It is recommended to add the following line manually:

Sitemap: https://example.com/sitemap.xml

This helps search engines (Google, Yandex, Bing, etc.) to discover your sitemap faster.

How can I limit taxonomy calculation for very large sites?

This is an advanced option, not required for normal sites.
By default, the plugin calculates <lastmod> for all selected taxonomy term archives (categories, tags, custom taxonomies) using a single optimized SQL query per taxonomy. This is safe and efficient in most cases.
However, on extremely large sites with tens of thousands of terms, you may want to set a soft cap to avoid heavy database operations.
You can do this with a simple filter in your theme’s functions.php or in a small custom plugin:

add_filter(‘lwsgp_tax_lastmod_cap’, function() {
return 5000; // maximum number of terms per taxonomy for
});

If the number of terms exceeds this cap, the plugin will still include the term URLs in the sitemap, but without <lastmod>. This prevents potential performance issues on very large sites.

Is dynamic mode dangerous or resource-hungry?

Not at all. Dynamic mode simply generates the sitemap on-the-fly, without writing a physical sitemap.xml file.
This is the same approach used by major SEO plugins (Yoast SEO, Rank Math, SEOPress) and even by the native WordPress sitemap feature (since WordPress 5.5).
With caching headers (ETag, Last-Modified) and browser/proxy cache, dynamic mode is safe and efficient. It is absolutely normal to use it, especially on hosting plans where file writing to the site root is not possible.

Should I include taxonomies (categories, tags, custom taxonomies) in the sitemap?

It depends. Taxonomies can generate a lot of additional URLs and each URL may add a small amount of load during sitemap generation.
For small and medium sites, this is not a problem, especially with bulk <lastmod> calculation (since version 1.0.3).
However, including every possible taxonomy “just in case” is usually unnecessary. Best practice is to enable only those taxonomies that are valuable for search engines and users (for example, categories in a blog, but not every tag). Always evaluate relevance rather than enabling everything by default.
sections.changelog:
1.0.5

  • I18N: Removed bundled .po/.mo files from the plugin package to avoid conflicts with community translations.
  • I18N: Improved language loading logic — plugin now prioritizes official WordPress.org translation packs (GlotPress). Falls back to local /languages folder only if no global translation exists.
  • UX: No functional changes. This release ensures consistent and up-to-date translations for all users.

1.0.4

  • UX: Added a quick “Generate / Update sitemap” button at the top of the settings screen (File mode only).
  • New: “Conservative” homepage mode — uses the modified time of the static front page (falls back to Smart if the homepage is the posts index).
  • Improved: “Smart” homepage now also considers ENABLED custom post types (detected) when calculating freshness. Custom taxonomies are intentionally ignored (performance-friendly).
  • I18N: Added a new translatable string for the “Conservative” mode.
  • No breaking changes. Fully backward-compatible with existing settings.

1.0.3

  • Performance: bulk calculation of taxonomy in a single SQL per taxonomy (massively faster on large sites).
  • Safety: optional soft cap for taxonomy via filter lwsgp_tax_lastmod_cap (default 0 = unlimited).
  • No breaking changes. Existing behavior preserved; features remain off by default.

1.0.2

  • New: support for any detected custom post types (CPT) and custom taxonomies — can be enabled in settings.
  • New: <lastmod> support for categories, tags, author archives, and date archives (based on the latest modified post).
  • Improved: admin UI now shows detected CPT/taxonomies with individual checkboxes (off by default).
  • Improved: translation support — added translators’ comments for placeholder strings.
  • Fixed: consistency of <lastmod> timestamps across all archive types.

1.0.1

  • Improved security: removed use of FILTER_UNSAFE_RAW, added stricter sanitization of server variables.
  • Added clearer HTTP diagnostic headers (including X-LWSGP-Cache: FILE for file mode).
  • Updated prefixes to avoid collisions (all code, options and transients now use lwsgp_).
  • General code cleanup and small stability fixes.

1.0.0

  • First stable release.
  • Added smart homepage <lastmod> calculation (blocks, WooCommerce, DW Q&A).
  • Added split mode (sitemapindex + multiple parts up to 50,000 URLs each).
  • Added better conflict detection and admin notices.
  • Added diagnostic headers and comments for easier debugging.
  • Improved caching in dynamic mode (ETag, Last-Modified, HIT/MISS).
  • Improved security checks and permission handling.
  • Many small fixes and code cleanup.
  • Based on previous 0.1 (initial release) and 0.2 (major improvements).
